The MAS-36 rifle hid its bayonet inside a compartment under the barrel instead of storing it separately — smart engineering that had one major flaw. Soldiers occasionally swapped bayonets between two rifles and locked them together permanently, unable to access the release catch. Later MAS-36 bayonets added a small access hole to fix this exact problem. Watch the full story of this WWII French rifle's ingenious (and flawed) bayonet system at Simple History.
